name: 24830-prefillheavy-opt125m-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
architecture: Dense decoder, OPTForCausalLM: 12 layers, hidden 768, 12 heads of head_dim 64, ffn_dim 3072, vocab 50272, max_position_embeddings 2048, torch_dtype float16, ~125M params (~0.25 GB fp16).
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=256, bounded at 20000 requests with a 1800 s safety cap, first 20% warmup by completion. The declared 10% cooldown is sized against the cap and does not fire, so the scored population is at least ~16000 requests.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets. Prompt EXACTLY 2000 tokens and output EXACTLY 48 (the backend sets ignore_eos when max_tokens is set), so 2048 is exactly the checkpoint's context. request_format MUST be `plain`: this tokenizer has no chat template.
purpose: A document-analysis assistant summarizing 2000-token passages into brief notes for 256 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
model: facebook/opt-125m
dtype: float16
swap-space: 16
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# LOAD-BEARING, not "the defaults": built through AsyncLLMEngine the library falls to
# 128 seqs and 2048 batched tokens, below the 256 streams scenario.json declares.
max-num-seqs: 1024
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

enable-prefix-caching: true

# HAZARD: do NOT add `disable-log-requests`. At this commit it is a deprecated read/write
# property rather than a dataclass field, so AsyncEngineArgs raises TypeError on it. Its
# replacement, enable_log_requests, already defaults False.
